incidente.resumo: In July 2017 a user impersonating a known developer had a technically valid package containing malicious code approved for inclusion in JCenter by reviewers who did not detect the impersonation; abuse reports sent in February 2018 apparently did not reach Bintray's monitoring. After a public blog post in December 2018, Bintray banned the fake user and removed the malicious packages and their links from JCenter.

descricao.texto: Community members reported the fake package as abuse through the Bintray reporting system in February 2018, but apparently, due to a technical failure, the reports did not reach the monitoring system; Bintray learned of the issue when it saw a blog post a reporter published in December 2018 raising it publicly.
trechos: In February 2018, according to Marton Braun, he and others reported the fake package as an abuse using the Bintray reporting system.
In December 2018, Marton published a blog post raising the issue to the public attention.

Once we saw the blog, we immediately banned the fake user from Bintray and removed the malicious packages created by them, including any links to these packages in JCenter (please see the list of the deleted files below).

gatilho.texto: In July 2017, a user impersonating a known developer asked to include a package in JCenter; the package was technically valid but contained malicious code.
trechos: In July 2017, a user impersonating Jake Wharton asked to include a package in JCenter.
The package was valid from a technical perspective (including sources and a license, etc), but also contained malicious code.

descricao.texto: The inclusion request review did not detect the impersonation and the package was approved for inclusion in JCenter; the inclusion process included steps to deal with impersonation attempts, which were not followed.
trechos: The Support team members who were reviewing the inclusion request failed to detect the impersonation and approved the package to be included in JCenter.
This process includes steps to deal with impersonation attempts, which were not followed.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Abuse reports sent through the Bintray reporting system in February 2018 apparently did not reach the monitoring system due to a technical failure, so the Bintray team did not receive them.
trechos: In February 2018, according to Marton Braun, he and others reported the fake package as an abuse using the Bintray reporting system.
Apparently these abuse report messages did not reach our monitoring system, due to a technical failure, causing the Bintray team not to receive the reports.

passos.texto: After seeing the blog post, Bintray banned the fake user and removed the malicious packages created by them, including any links to these packages in JCenter.
trechos: Once we saw the blog, we immediately banned the fake user from Bintray and removed the malicious packages created by them, including any links to these packages in JCenter (please see the list of the deleted files below).

acoes.texto: Already done: improved observability of the reporting system by adding monitoring alerts and more logs.
trechos: We improved the observability of the reporting system by adding monitoring alerts and more logs.

acoes.texto: Already done: refreshed the inclusion request process, which includes steps to deal with impersonation attempts, with the Support team.
trechos: We have refreshed the inclusion request process with the Support team. This process includes steps to deal with impersonation attempts, which were not followed.

acoes.texto: In progress: creating a dedicated moderation team for closer inspection of inclusion requests, including investigation and validation of authors and their claims on the namespace of published content.
trechos: In parallel, we are creating a dedicated moderation team to focus primarily on closer inspection and moderation of inclusion requests, including investigation and validation of authors and their claims on the namespace of published content.

acoes.texto: Swift turnaround for community moderation signals from the Bintray reporting system and from social channels such as Twitter.
trechos: Swift turnaround for community moderation signals, coming not only from the Bintray reporting system but also from social channels, such as Twitter, etc.

observacoes: The malicious package was available in JCenter from its approval (the inclusion request was made in July 2017; the approval date is not given) until its removal after the December 2018 blog post; no bounded outage duration applies. The postmortem was posted Jan 16, 2019 and a 'Resolved' update Dec 12, 2018. The document ends with the list of files uploaded by the fake user. categoria_causa is human-error rather than supply-chain because the stated root cause is the approval of the impersonated inclusion request, not the tampering itself.
